A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal-graph characterization and learning framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original ADMG enumeration and sampling experiments comparing hard- and soft-intervention equivalence classes, with results in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the Section 7 experiments and adds simulated binary and linear Gaussian comparisons with GIES and IGSP in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes the stored separating sets for F-to-observed-node pairs by adding the set of F nodes alongside the conditioning variables and intervention targets. The overall graph construction, learning objective, and orientation rules remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds finite-sample causal discovery on binary and linear Gaussian data from a small latent-confounded graph. This extends the empirical coverage beyond graph enumeration and equivalence-class sampling, although the graph structure already appeared as a theoretical example in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix D newly reports evaluated outputs from GIES and IGSP in a limited illustrative comparison. Section 7 retains its comparison with the soft-intervention characterization of Kocaoglu et al. (2019); discussion of I-FCI, psi-FCI, and JCI does not establish additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D comparison specifies 100,000 observational samples and 100,000 samples under intervention on Z, then considers a linear Gaussian counterpart under the same setting. These are added protocols; the graph-generation settings, intervention selection, and estimation procedures underlying Tables 1–4 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a comparative case study examining incorrect causal order, observational equivalence, and missing latent-confounder information in baseline outputs. The hard-versus-soft counterexamples and algorithm-incompleteness example already appeared in v1 Appendix A.8 and are retained in v2 E.3–E.4.

E5.justification: The existing 30- and 50-ground-truth-graph sampling designs, uncertainty displays, and Hoeffding-based estimation remain unchanged. Appendix D adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. Appendix D newly reports that binary-data GIES returns Y → Z → X, whereas IGSP returns X → Z → Y with X → Y; both return X → Z → Y in the Gaussian case. It reports the proposed method recovering the graphs in Figure 3k in both settings.

T1.justification: Compared with v1 A.6, Appendix B.5 adds a separating-set validity argument covering unshielded colliders and discriminating paths. Appendix E.2 adds complexity reasoning, including an O(kn^5) claim motivated by restricting conditioning-set size. The central equivalence and soundness theorem statements are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalized do-calculus constraints, graphical characterization of hard-intervention equivalence with latent variables, and a sound learning algorithm with new orientation rules.

C2.justification: New discussions explain positivity, the relationship between h-faithfulness and ordinary faithfulness, and finite-sample testing difficulties. Appendix F explicitly identifies interpretability costs of graph tuples and reliance on full interventional distributions. Algorithm incompleteness and exceptions to hard interventions being more informative were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly identifies the Python GIES implementation and the causaldag implementation of IGSP; the GIES reference includes commit e13f9a7. These improve baseline implementation traceability, although generative parameters and statistical-test settings for the new comparison remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Appendices A and D substantially expand comparative positioning through explicit contrasts of output representations, latent-variable assumptions, and claimed guarantees across I-FCI, psi-FCI, JCI, GIES, and IGSP. New citations also support discussions of faithfulness, identification, Bayesian discovery, and applications. This extends the substantive comparison with prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes Appendix A.1–A.8 into named appendices, groups proofs under Appendix B, and adds an appendix contents page. It also centralizes notation, adds explanatory footnotes, corrects wording, and updates affiliations. The main narrative and ordering of retained material remain largely intact.

P2.justification: All six figures and four tables are retained. Figure 5 has a revised panel arrangement, domain superscripts are corrected in Figures 5 and 6, and some captions are corrected. Tables and algorithm boxes use lighter rules, with accompanying changes in placement and page layout.

improvement.justification: The added separating-set reasoning, explicit discussion of assumptions and practical limits, and corrected figure labels make v2 easier to assess. The empirical addition remains a small illustration with incomplete implementation settings, and the polynomial complexity claim relies on a conditioning-set restriction absent from the printed exhaustive algorithm. With the central theorems and main numerical evidence unchanged, the gains support a limited overall improvement.
